english: Let $S$ denote the set of all real numbers $x$ satisfying $2\sin^{-1}(\sin x)=\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{20}\right)$, where the inverse trigonometric functions take their principal values. Then the number of elements in $S$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $S$ उन सभी वास्तविक संख्याओं $x$ का समुच्चय है जो $2\sin^{-1}(\sin x)=\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{20}\right)$ को संतुष्ट करती हैं, जहाँ प्रतिलोम त्रिकोणमितीय फलन अपने मुख्य मान लेते हैं। तब $S$ में अवयवों की संख्या ______ है।
solution: Domain: $\left|\dfrac{x}{20}\right|\le1\Rightarrow x\in[-20,20]$. Range: RHS $\in[0,\pi]$, so $f(x)=\sin^{-1}(\sin x)$ must equal $g(x)=\dfrac12\cos^{-1}\dfrac{x}{20}\in\left[0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$

$f\ge0$ only on humps $[2k\pi,(2k+1)\pi]$, where $f$ rises from $0$ to $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ (at the midpoint) and falls back to $0$; $g$ decreases from $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ to $0$ with $0<g<\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ on $(-20,20)$
On each: $f-g<0$ at both ends and $>0$ at the midpoint; $f-g$ is strictly monotonic on each half ($|g'|=\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{400-x^{2}}}<1$ there), so 2 roots per hump $\Rightarrow12$
Partial hump $[6\pi,20]$: $f=x-6\pi$ rises $0\to1.15$, $g$ falls $0.17\to0$: 1 root. On $[-20,-6\pi]$, $f<0$: none
solution_full: Domain. $\cos^{-1}\dfrac{x}{20}$ is defined only for $-20\le x\le20$; $\sin^{-1}(\sin x)$ is defined for all $x$. So every solution lies in $[-20,20]$.

Range. $\cos^{-1}\dfrac{x}{20}\in[0,\pi]$, so a solution needs $2\sin^{-1}(\sin x)\in[0,\pi]$, that is $f(x)=\sin^{-1}(\sin x)\in\left[0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$. Write the equation as $f(x)=g(x)$ with $g(x)=\dfrac12\cos^{-1}\dfrac{x}{20}$.

Graph of $f$: a triangle wave of period $2\pi$ with $f(x)=x-2k\pi$ on $\left[2k\pi-\dfrac{\pi}{2},2k\pi+\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$ and $f(x)=(2k+1)\pi-x$ on $\left[2k\pi+\dfrac{\pi}{2},2k\pi+\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right]$. So $f\ge0$ exactly on the humps $[2k\pi,(2k+1)\pi]$, rising from $0$ to $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and back to $0$.

Graph of $g$: strictly decreasing from $g(-20)=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ to $g(20)=0$, and $0<g<\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ for $-20<x<20$. Its slope is $g'(x)=-\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{400-x^{2}}}$, with $|g'|<1$ whenever $\sqrt{400-x^{2}}>\dfrac12$, that is for all $|x|<19.99$.

On such a hump, $h=f-g$ satisfies $h=-g<0$ at both ends and $h=\dfrac{\pi}{2}-g>0$ at the midpoint. On the rising half $h'=1-g'>0$; on the falling half $h'=-1-g'=-1+|g'|<0$. So $h$ has exactly one zero on each half: 2 solutions per hump, 12 in all.

Partial hump $[6\pi,20]$ ($6\pi\approx18.85$, $7\pi>20$): here $f(x)=x-6\pi$ increases from $0$ to $20-6\pi\approx1.15<\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, while $g$ decreases from $g(6\pi)\approx0.17$ to $0$. Then $h$ is increasing, negative at $6\pi$ and positive at $20$: exactly 1 solution.
On $[-20,-6\pi)$, $x+6\pi\in[-1.15,0)$ so $f(x)=x+6\pi<0\le g(x)$: no solution. Between humps $f<0$: no solution.
originality_note: New: a triangle wave of doubled amplitude is matched against an inverse cosine whose domain [-20,20] fixes the window and whose range [0,pi] removes every negative part of the wave, leaving two roots per hump plus one in a partial hump (way 5). Closest known: number of solutions of sin^-1(sin x) = x/k or of sqrt(1+cos2x) = sqrt2 tan^-1(tan x). Different because: the right side is itself an inverse trigonometric function, so domain and range both cut the count.

concept_use.Domain and range of inverse trigonometri: Domain of cos^-1(x/20) restricts x to [-20,20]; its range [0,pi] forces sin^-1(sin x) into [0,pi/2], discarding the negative parts of the wave.
concept_use.Graphs of inverse trigonometric function: The counting is read from the triangle-wave graph of sin^-1(sin x) against the decreasing graph of (1/2)cos^-1(x/20).

stem_review: Read as a student: every function has a stated domain, every symbol is introduced before use, principal values are stated, every condition is given, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed with mpmath/numpy and is unique and equal to the Answer Plan; no hyperbolic functions or asymptotes. Checked numerically (2 million sample points) that there are exactly 13 sign changes and no tangency; x = -20 is not a solution. Changed: No change.
key_step: Using domain and range of cos^-1(x/20) to restrict to the non-negative humps of sin^-1(sin x) in [-20,20] and counting two crossings per full hump plus one in the partial hump.
justification: Graph-based counting with domain and range restrictions and an edge-interval check, numerical answer with no options. Two ideas linked; comparable to 2025-P2-Q3 (L3) count of solutions of an ITF equation and above 2023-P1-Q8 (L2).
